# `⌈` — Ceiling / Maximum

Function. Keys: `Alt-s`. Hanzi: `上`. Ranks: `0` monadic, `0 0` dyadic

`⌈Y` rounds up to an exact integer. Pervasive; tolerant near integers. An infinity or NaN stays a float. Complex ceiling is `-⌊-Y`.

```bpl
⌈1.2 ¯1.2         ⍝ [2 ¯1]ₓ
⌈3r2              ⍝ 2ₓ
```

`X⌈Y` takes the real maximum, and for characters the one with the higher code point. A character is greater than any number, as [`⍋`](delta-stile.qmd) orders them. Pervasive. A NaN beside any number gives NaN, in either order and on every machine. A reduction or scan gives NaN from its first NaN on. To leave NaNs out, remove them first, as in `⌈/(v=v)#v`. Empty reduction identity: `¯∞`.

```bpl
3⌈1 5             ⍝ 3 5
3⌈1 $n 5          ⍝ 3 $n 5
⌈\1 $n 3          ⍝ 1 $n $n
"abc"⌈"bab"       ⍝ "bbc"
3⌈'a'             ⍝ 'a'
```
